title: Amazon Leo is bringing high-quality satellite internet to Uzbekistan
summary: Amazon Leo has partnered with telecoms leader Uztelecom to extend connectivity where it’s needed most.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon Leo will power satellite connectivity in remote and hard-to-reach regions of Uzbekistan.


- Uztelecom affiliate UZ-SAT will serve as an authorized distributor of Amazon Leo.


- The agreement advances the country's goal of building a unified digital environment that reaches every community.


---


[Amazon Leo](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/amazon-leo) has announced a new agreement that will expand internet connectivity across Uzbekistan.


UZ-SAT, a subsidiary of Uztelecom, the country’s leading telecommunications operator, will serve as an authorized distributor of Amazon Leo. UZ-SAT will use Amazon Leo to create and deliver new connectivity solutions to its customers, bringing fast, reliable satellite internet to communities and businesses in areas where traditional networks are difficult to deploy.


[Amazon Leo introduces gigabit-speed antenna for commercial aviation](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-leo/amazon-leo-aviation-antenna-gigabit-wifi)


The Amazon Leo Aviation Antenna will deliver reliable internet connectivity to airline passengers and crew with up to 1 Gbps download and 400 Mbps upload speeds.


Uztelecom currently provides connectivity to 96% of communities, operates more than 234,000 miles (378,000 kilometers) of fiber-optic infrastructure, and serves more than 13 million users. Despite that extensive reach, Uzbekistan's diverse geography—from mountain regions to remote desert communities—means some areas remain difficult and costly to connect through terrestrial networks alone. Amazon Leo is designed to complement Uztelecom's existing infrastructure, extending connectivity where it is needed most.


## How Amazon Leo brings connectivity to remote areas


Amazon Leo is designed to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers beyond the reach of traditional networks. The system is powered by an initial constellation of more than


[3,000 satellites](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-leo/amazon-leo-direct-to-device-satellite-service-explained) connected to a secure, global network of ground gateway antennas and dedicated fiber infrastructure. A range of customer terminals—Amazon Leo Nano, Pro, and Ultra—are designed to make connectivity simple to deploy across a range of use cases.


[Amazon Leo set to accelerate satellite production and launch cadence](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/amazon-leo/amazon-leo-plans-double-launch-rate-20-missions)


Amazon Leo plans to double its annual launch rate as it prepares for initial service rollout.


"We're excited to bring Amazon Leo to Uzbekistan, delivering high-performance connectivity to communities and businesses that need it most. Collaborations like our agreement with Uztelecom and UZ-SAT are essential to making this a reality—combining our satellite technology with local expertise to open new doors for economic growth, education, and innovation in more places around the world," said Trevor Vieweg, global head of business for Amazon Leo.


## Supporting Uzbekistan’s digital transformation


The agreement was announced during the 5th Tashkent International Investment Forum on the first day of ICT Week Uzbekistan 2026 and comes as Uzbekistan is driving an ambitious digital transformation across the country, investing in modern infrastructure and building a connected digital economy.


"Working with Amazon Leo will enable us to expand connectivity options in areas where the deployment of traditional terrestrial infrastructure is limited. Our goal is to make modern digital technologies more accessible, regardless of where people live or work. Next-generation satellite connectivity will complement Uztelecom's existing infrastructure and provide another important tool for advancing Uzbekistan's digital development," said Bakhrom Azimov, general director of UZ-SAT.


Amazon Leo has launched nearly 400 satellites to date and is currently testing the service with employees and with select enterprise customers as part of a private preview. We expect to begin rolling out initial service in certain locations later this year, and will expand coverage as we launch more satellites and add coverage and capacity to the network.


To learn more and sign up for updates, visit


[leo.amazon.com](https://leo.amazon.com/) .
